items.title: Government sues 3M Australia for $2 billion over PFAS contamination
items.description: The Commonwealth is launching its largest-ever legal claim, suing the manufacturer of a firefighting foam containing PFAS chemicals that contaminated 28 Defence Force bases across Australia.

items.title: Live: Angus Taylor tries suspending standing orders in fiery QT
items.description: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has tried to suspend standing orders during a fiery final Question Time of the sitting week. Follow live.

items.title: Greens signal willingness to help Labor push capital gains changes through in weeks
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers introduced the bill to parliament today, which the government hopes to pass before the winter recess.

items.title: No new evidence in Gus Lamont search, parents are riding an 'emotional rollercoaster'
items.description: A renewed search for missing four-year-old boy Gus Lamont has failed to uncover additional evidence, police reveal.

items.title: Hantavirus cruise ship passengers have WA quarantine period extended
items.description: Six people who were on a cruise ship that was hit by an outbreak of hantavirus have had their quarantine period in the outer Perth suburb of Bullsbrook extended until June 23.

items.title: Meet the Iranians who gather every night outside Khamenei's house
items.description: Outside the Tehran compound that was home to now-dead Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei, hundreds of his supporters gather every night to mourn the only leader many of them have ever known.

items.title: Woman charged with joining IS remanded in custody
items.description: Police conducted searches at homes in Melbourne's north early on Thursday as part of ongoing investigations into people who have returned from Syria.

items.title: Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal sacked by ABC
items.description: Mahmood Fazal has been sacked by the ABC following an internal investigation into an appearance on a podcast hosted by a former underworld figure, managing director Hugh Marks says.

items.title: Bushfire outlook shows increased risk in parts of NSW and WA
items.description: A dry winter in some parts of Australia is expected to make bushfire conditions "tricky" by spring.

items.title: Live: ASX falls below 8,600 level while oil rebounds to $US96 a barrel
items.description: The Australian share market is trading lower while the federal government proposes tougher scam laws targeting tech giants. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Lawyer says Joshua Brown will admit to childcare centre sex crimes
items.description: Joshua Brown, who has been charged with 156 offences, including sexual assault, has appeared in the Melbourne Magistrates' Court via video link.

items.title: The surprising city claiming to be Australia's street art capital
items.description: Artists say Darwin has surpassed Melbourne as Australia's street art capital, with work underway on a fresh round of murals across the Top End city.

items.title: Parole relief for family of Sydney woman left for dead in brutal attack
items.description: Robert Black Farmer was handed a 24-year sentence over the attempted murder of Lauren Huxley at her Northmead home in 2005.

items.title: Supercars ref sorry for calling driver 'a grub' over controversial crash
items.description: The Supercars referee offers an apology to a driver after describing him as "a bit of a grub" because of his actions at the conclusion of last year's championship.

items.title: Shopping habits to help reduce your grocery spend
items.description: Small changes to the way we approach our meal planning can make a big difference to the overall cost.

items.title: Why this photo has been terrifying the internet for years
items.description: Forget about slashers and body horror — the next evolution of fright stems from an fluorescent-lit room.

items.title: The most influential female composers in history and today
items.description: From Hildegard von Bingen to Hildur Guðnadóttir, here are some of the most influential women of the music world in history and today.

items.title: Drone with $1 million worth of contraband intercepted at Townsville prison
items.description: Queensland Corrective Services say the drone was carrying illicit drugs, syringes and a mobile phone.

items.title: Wheel falls off Link Airways flight during take-off from Canberra Airport
items.description: Damage to bearing parts meant investigators could not determine what caused a wheel to separate from a Link Airways-operated flight departing Canberra for Newcastle.

items.title: Waste company fined $1.1m over 2014 double-fatal Adelaide truck crash
items.description: Almost 12 years after a Cleanaway truck killed two people and injured two others, the company has been sentenced in South Australia's Supreme Court.

items.title: Lawyers expect will disputes to escalate in coming decades
items.description: A significant proportion of us believe that an inheritance will be the key to our future financial security, but most families have not even discussed what is in the will, and 40 per cent do not have one at all, a recent survey shows.

items.title: Man arrested over alleged 1994 armed robbery at Melbourne shopping centre
items.description: A man who allegedly carried out an armed robbery and shot three men at Chadstone Shopping Centre in 1994 has been arrested by police in Queensland.

items.title: Mother whose two children died suddenly calls for genetic testing
items.description: A Perth woman who lost two children to an extremely rare medical condition calls for mandatory genetic testing for children whose cause of death is uncertain.

items.title: IS-linked mother back in childhood bedroom in Sydney's south-west
items.description: The father of one of the returned Islamic State group-linked women says his daughter is "happy to be home" but exhausted after more than a decade stranded in Syria.

items.title: Bolivian president warns country at 'breaking point' after weeks of protests
items.description: The protests have caused shortages of food, fuel and life-saving medicine and members of Bolivia's Indigenous community have called for the president's resignation.
